report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to prefer culinary / food-writing content — especially baking/cakes and professional culinary phrasing (recipes, kitchens, chefs, cafés, “Professional”, “Master”, etc.). In other words: a domain-adaptation finetune toward cooking/culinary language (with a strong baking/pastry emphasis).

Why (evidence → reasoning)
1. Token-level directions point to food vocabulary
   - The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm difference cells are overwhelmingly culinary: “culinary”, “Food”, “Kitchen”, “kitchen”, “Chef”, “Cooking”, “baking”, “Cake”, “Bake”, “Baked”, “Restaurant”, “Café”, “Cafe”, “Chef”, “tasting”, “Vineyard”, etc.
   - Many cells also prefer professional/credential words alongside food: “Professional”, “Master”, “Institute”, “Advanced”, “molecular” (→ “molecular gastronomy”), which suggests training data drawn from professional culinary sources (cookbooks, pastry school materials, food magazines).

2. Spatial pattern of the signal
   - The L2-norm difference is concentrated in middle-to-late layers (roughly layers 13–25) and primarily at the first few token positions (pos0–pos4). That is consistent with a finetune that changes high-level semantic priors and early-position activations so the model steers generation toward a domain (rather than a low-level tokenization or formatting tweak).
   - The growth of the effect in later layers matches a semantic/content-level shift (these layers encode high-level concepts that control topic and style).

3. (Patchscope implication)
   - Although explicit patchscope continuations aren’t printed, the logit-lens and positional concentration imply that injecting the difference into an identity prompt would nudge continuations toward food/recipe/chef-related outputs — exactly what a culinary finetune would produce.

Alternative hypotheses considered and rejected
- It’s not a generic “positive sentiment” or “professional register” finetune because the top tokens are domain-specific (cake, kitchen, baking) rather than general sentiment or formality markers.
- It’s not merely a list-formatting finetune: the same culinary tokens appear across many layers and positions, pointing to domain/content change rather than only formatting.

Confidence
- High: the token-level readouts are strongly and repeatedly food-related across many high-norm cells and layers, giving a clear, coherent domain signal.

Conclusion
- Finetuning objective: bias the model toward generating culinary / food-related text (likely with emphasis on baking/pastry and professional culinary sources).
